web.extension.name: Website
web.extension.description: HTTPS redirection, HSTS, CSP and the other protection headers, security.txt.
web.no_website: No website on the domain or on www: this check does not apply.
web.https_redirect.title: Automatic switch to HTTPS
web.https_redirect.why: A visitor who types the address without "https://" must be sent to the encrypted version. Otherwise they browse in clear text: their forms can be read and the page changed on the way.
web.https_redirect.ref: ANSSI, « Recommandations pour la sécurisation des sites web »
web.https_redirect.missing: http://{host} shows the website without encryption instead of redirecting to HTTPS.
web.https_redirect.message:
Hello,

The address http://{host} shows the website without encryption. Could you add a permanent (301) redirect from http:// to https:// for every page?

Thank you.
web.https_redirect.ok: Visitors are always sent to HTTPS.
web.https_redirect.external: http://{host} redirects to another website, but https://{host} refuses the connection: the audited domain has no HTTPS of its own.
web.https_redirect.bad_certificate: The HTTPS destination for {host} has an invalid or untrusted certificate.
web.https_redirect.https_unavailable: The HTTPS destination for {host} refuses connections: HTTPS is not confirmed.
web.hsts.title: HTTPS required (HSTS)
web.hsts.why: HSTS asks browsers to use only HTTPS for the website for a given time, even if a link or a rigged network offers http://.
web.hsts.ref: RFC 6797 · ANSSI, « Recommandations pour la sécurisation des sites web »
web.hsts.short: The HSTS duration of {host} is short ({days:day|days}): at least six months are recommended.
web.hsts.message:
Hello,

Could you add the following header on {host}, on every HTTPS response:

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000

Thank you.
web.hsts.ok: HSTS is on, with a long enough duration.
web.hsts.invalid: The HSTS header of {host} has no readable "max-age": browsers ignore it.
web.hsts.disabled: The HSTS header of {host} has a zero duration (max-age=0): it tells browsers to forget the protection.
web.csp.title: Content Security Policy (CSP)
web.csp.why: The CSP tells the browser where the website may load its scripts from. A script injected by an attacker is then blocked instead of running for your visitors.
web.csp.message:
Hello,

The website {host} sends no Content-Security-Policy header. Could you set one up, first in "Report-Only" mode so nothing breaks, then in blocking mode?

Thank you.
web.csp.ok: A Content Security Policy is in place.
web.csp.no_script: The content security policy of {host} does not restrict scripts (neither script-src nor default-src).
web.csp.unsafe_inline: The content security policy of {host} allows scripts written in the page ('unsafe-inline'): an injected script would still run.
web.csp.open: The content security policy of {host} allows scripts from any origin (*, https: or data:).
web.framing.title: Protection against framing (clickjacking)
web.framing.action: Forbid framing the website in other pages
web.framing.why: Without this protection, a rigged website can show yours invisibly and make your visitors click without knowing it.
web.framing.missing: {host} can be shown inside a third-party page.
web.framing.message:
Hello,

Could you add on {host} the header "X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN" (or the CSP directive "frame-ancestors 'self'")?

Thank you.
web.framing.ok: The website cannot be framed by a third-party page.
web.framing.permissive: The frame-ancestors directive of {host} lets any site show yours in a page (browsers then ignore X-Frame-Options).
web.framing.obsolete: {host} uses "X-Frame-Options: ALLOW-FROM", which current browsers no longer understand: the site can be shown in a third-party page.
web.nosniff.title: File types respected (nosniff)
web.nosniff.why: This header stops the browser from guessing the type of a file, a guess that can turn a file uploaded by a visitor into a script.
web.nosniff.message:
Hello,

Could you add on {host} the header "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff"?

Thank you.
web.nosniff.ok: The browser respects the announced type of files.
web.referrer.title: Referring address (Referrer-Policy)
web.referrer.why: When a visitor follows an outgoing link, the browser may send the full address of the page they leave, sometimes with personal information in it.
web.referrer.missing: {host} sets no Referrer-Policy. Recent browsers apply a careful default; older ones send the full address.
web.referrer.message:
Hello,

Could you add on {host} the header "Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin"?

Thank you.
web.referrer.ok: Sending the referring address is restricted.
web.referrer.unsafe: {host} asks browsers to send the full address of its pages to every site, even without encryption (Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url).
web.server_banner.title: Software versions shown
web.server_banner.why: Showing the exact version of the server tells attackers which known flaws to try first.
web.server_banner.ref: ANSSI, « Recommandations pour la sécurisation des sites web »
web.server_banner.message:
Hello,

The website of {domain} shows its software version in the header "{header}" ("{value}"). Could you hide it?

Thank you.
web.security_txt.title: Security contact (security.txt)
web.security_txt.why: The security.txt file says whom to tell about a flaw found on the website. Without it, whoever finds one does not know whom to write to.
web.security_txt.message:
Hello,

Could you publish the file https://{domain}/.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116) with at least a line "Contact: mailto:security@{domain}" and a line "Expires:"?

Thank you.
web.security_txt.ok: A valid security.txt file gives a contact.
web.security_txt.invalid: The file {url} is incomplete: {fields} is missing (fields required by RFC 9116).
web.security_txt.expired: The file {url} expired on {expires_on}: its information is no longer considered current.
web.https_redirect.external.message:
Hello,

http://{host} redirects to another website, but https://{host}/ refuses the connection: https:// links and bookmarks do not work.

Could you open HTTPS on {host}, with a valid certificate, and have the same redirect start from https://{host}/?

Thank you.
web.https_redirect.external.why: Without HTTPS on {host}, https:// addresses (links, bookmarks, browsers that try HTTPS first) lead nowhere: only the unencrypted version redirects to the other website.
web.https_redirect.refused: From the scanner, HTTPS is refused by {host} on all its published addresses ({addresses}): visitors cannot open the website over https://.
web.https_redirect.refused_partial: From the scanner, HTTPS is refused by {host} on some of its addresses ({addresses}): visitors sent to them cannot open the website.
web.https_redirect.refused_partial.actio: Restore HTTPS on every address of {host}
web.https_redirect.refused_undetermined: From the scanner, HTTPS is refused by {host} on {tested:tested address|tested addresses} ({addresses}) out of {published} published; {untested:other one gave|others gave} no conclusive result.
web.https_redirect.obsolete: {host} accepts HTTPS only over obsolete TLS ({versions}) on all its addresses ({addresses}): no current browser can open the website.
web.https_redirect.obsolete_partial: On {host}, HTTPS is accepted only over obsolete TLS on some addresses ({addresses}): visitors sent to them cannot open the website.
web.https_redirect.obsolete_partial.acti: Enable TLS 1.2 and 1.3 on every address of {host}
web.https_redirect.obsolete_undetermined: On {host}, HTTPS is accepted only over obsolete TLS on {tested:tested address|tested addresses} ({addresses}) out of {published} published; {untested:other one gave|others gave} no conclusive result.
web.https_redirect.no_service: No web service answers on {host} ({addresses}): neither HTTP nor HTTPS. If this name no longer serves a website, remove its address from the DNS; otherwise, restore HTTPS.
web.https_redirect.no_service.action: Restore HTTPS on {host}, or remove its address
web.https_redirect.unknown: Not evaluated: no address of {host} gave a conclusive HTTPS answer.
web.https_redirect.budget: Not evaluated: the HTTPS probe reached its {seconds}-second deadline before concluding for {host}.
web.https_redirect.legacy_untestable: Not evaluated: {host} refuses TLS 1.2 and 1.3, and the scanner cannot try TLS 1.0 or 1.1 to find out whether it still accepts them.
web.https_redirect.untestable: Not evaluated: the addresses of {host} ({addresses}) could not be tested from the scanner.
web.https_redirect.http_unknown: Not evaluated: http://{host} answered on no address.
web.https_redirect.refused.message:
Hello,

From our audit tool, HTTPS on {host} is refused ({addresses}). Could you serve this name over HTTPS with a valid certificate, or, if it no longer serves a website, remove its address from the DNS?

Thank you.
web.https_redirect.restore.message:
Hello,

From our audit tool, HTTPS on {host} is refused ({addresses}), while the website announces HTTPS: visitors who received that announcement can no longer open it. Could you restore HTTPS on this name, with a valid certificate?

Thank you.
web.https_redirect.verify.message:
Hello,

From our audit tool, HTTPS on {host} is refused ({addresses}), and the cause could not be located. Could you check HTTPS on this name from another network before changing anything?

Thank you.
web.https_redirect.obsolete.message:
Hello,

The web server of {host} ({addresses}) accepts HTTPS only over TLS 1.0 or 1.1, versions current browsers refuse. Could you enable TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3?

Thank you.
web.https_redirect.note.external: http://{host} redirects to {target}, another website: the target is noted, never contacted, and is not an announcement of HTTPS.
web.https_redirect.note.certificate: The validity of the certificate is judged by the “Website certificate” check.
web.https_redirect.note.default_offer: Default TLS offer refused by {addresses}: TLS 1.2 alone goes through.
web.https_redirect.note.discovery: Incomplete discovery: looking up the addresses of {hosts} did not succeed.
web.https_redirect.note.sample: Sample limited to 4 addresses per family: {count:address not tested|addresses not tested} ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.note.deadline: Probe stopped at its {seconds}-second deadline: {count:address unfinished|addresses unfinished} ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.note.no_route: {count:address not tested|addresses not tested} from the scanner, no route ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.note.legacy: {count:address refuses|addresses refuse} TLS 1.2 and 1.3 while the scanner cannot try TLS 1.0 or 1.1 ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.note.policy: {count:address excluded|addresses excluded} by the scan's network rule ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.note.timeout: {count:address without a conclusive answer|addresses without a conclusive answer} ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.note.no_http: {count:address negotiates|addresses negotiate} TLS without answering in HTTP ({addresses}).
web.https_redirect.attribution.undetermi: From the scanner, HTTPS on {host} is refused. The cause could not be located: it may come from the destination or from the scanner's network path.
web.https_redirect.attribution.destinati: From the scanner, HTTPS on {host} is refused. Another TLS negotiation of the domain succeeded from the scanner ({other}): the refusal is specific to {address} for this name. The scan does not tell whether it comes from the server or from equipment placed in front of it.
web.https_redirect.attribution.name: From the scanner, HTTPS on {host} is refused. Another TLS negotiation succeeded on the same address for another name ({other}): the refusal is specific to this name on this address. The scan does not tell whether it comes from the server or from equipment placed in front of it.
web.https_redirect.announced.redirect: HTTPS is announced for {host}: http:// redirects there to HTTPS of the same name.
web.https_redirect.announced.hints: Indication: a DNS HTTPS record is published for {host}.
web.note.obsolete_page: Page served only over obsolete TLS ({addresses}): current browsers do not reach it.
web.note.name_mismatch: The certificate presented does not carry the name {host}: the page read may be the server's default website.
web.hsts.note.invalid_certificate: The HSTS header of {host} comes with an invalid certificate: browsers ignore it.
web.security_txt.note.unverifiable: security.txt is served with an invalid certificate: a researcher cannot verify where it comes from.
web.https_redirect.refused_undetermined_: From the scanner, HTTPS is refused by {host} on {tested:tested address|tested addresses} ({addresses}); looking up its other addresses did not succeed.
web.https_redirect.obsolete_undetermined: On {host}, HTTPS is accepted only over obsolete TLS on {tested:tested address|tested addresses} ({addresses}); looking up its other addresses did not succeed.
web.https_redirect.announced.hsts_histor: An authenticated, unexpired HSTS policy announces HTTPS for {host}.
web.https_redirect.announced.https_histo: Hint for {host}: HTTPS answered in a previous scan; this does not establish current availability.
web.https_redirect.announced.preload: Hint for {host}: the header requests preloading; the preload list is not consulted.
